title: Remote Land Due Diligence in Bangladesh: How Expats in USA, UK & Canada Can Verify Khatians & Namjari Online (2026)
metaTitle: Verify Land in Bangladesh from Abroad: NRB Title Search Guide 2026
metaDescription: Exhaustive legal manual for NRBs in USA, UK & Canada to verify CS, SA, RS, BS Khatians, e-Namjari, and fake Dalils in Bangladesh online before buying or investing.
keywords: check bangladesh land record online from abroad
legal vetting of property in bangladesh
non encumbrance certificate nec sub registry
heroIntro: Hard-earned foreign remittances earned through years of labor by Non-Resident Bangladeshis (NRBs) in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia are frequently targeted by predatory housing societies, rogue real estate developers, and unscrupulous relatives selling disputed, encumbered, or non-existent land. In Bangladesh's real estate ecosystem, physical possession does NOT guarantee legal title. Fraudulent sellers routinely manufacture counterfeit deeds (ভুয়া দলিল), forge mutation slips, sell mortgaged plots, or sell the same parcel to multiple overseas buyers. Thanks to Bangladesh's modernized digital land governance (land.gov.bd, e-Porcha, and DLRS map portals), overseas investors can now conduct rigorous preliminary due diligence from London, New York, or Toronto. However, digital checks cover only half the risk; sealing an investment demands physical Sub-Registry Volume Book searches, Non-Encumbrance Certificate (NEC) audits, and a formal written **Title Search & Legal Opinion Report (স্বত্ব মতামত প্রতিবেদন)** by an enrolled Supreme Court advocate. This exhaustive guide provides the complete legal vetting blueprint for overseas property investors.

quickAnswer.heading: Remote Property Due Diligence: 6 Cardinal Steps
points: Trace the 25-Year Chain of Title (বায়া দলিল / Baya Dalil) unbroken from the original CS or SA Khatian to the present owner.
Verify digital Khatians (CS, SA, RS, BS / City Survey) online via the Ministry of Land portal (eporcha.gov.bd).
Cross-verify the seller's e-Namjari (ই-নামজারি) mutation and DCR receipt on mutation.land.gov.bd to ensure it is not a forged manual slip.
Inspect up-to-date Land Development Tax payment dakhilas at ldtax.gov.bd to verify active government rent roll status.
Conduct physical Volume Book (বালাম বই) searches and apply for a Non-Encumbrance Certificate (NEC Form 41) at the Sub-Registry Office.
Verify that the plot does NOT fall under government Khas, Vested Property ('Ka' Schedule), Waqf, Forest land, or RAJUK master-plan acquisition.
Insist on an Advocate Legal Search & Marketable Title Report before transferring any booking money or signing contracts.

sections.h2: 1. The Core Peril: Why Physical Possession Does Not Mean Legal Title in Bangladesh
sections.content:
In Western real estate markets (USA, UK, Canada), title guarantees and title insurance protect buyers from hidden encumbrances or defective registries. In Bangladesh, the doctrine of Caveat Emptor (ক্রেতা সাবধান / Buyer Beware) applies with absolute rigor.

A seller can physically stand on a plot in Dhaka or Sylhet, show you boundary walls, and introduce local caretakers, while possessing zero marketable title in law. Common fraudulent traps targeting expatriates include:

  • Secret Bank Mortgages: The seller deposited the original title deeds with a commercial bank to secure a BDT 5 Crore loan, then used a 'lost deed' police GD to obtain a certified copy and sell the land to an unsuspecting expat.
  • Double Sale (একাধিক বিক্রয়): The seller executed a registered deed to Buyer A, and before Buyer A completed mutation, hurriedly sold the identical Dag/plot to an overseas Buyer B.
  • Un-Partitioned Joint Land: Selling a specific road-facing plot that legally belongs to an undivided ancestral estate where other co-sharers have not partitioned.
  • Unapproved Developer Projects: Private housing companies carving up low-lying flood retention zones without RAJUK or DOE clearance.

sections.h2: 2. The 25-Year Unbroken Chain of Title (বায়া দলিল / Baya Dalil) Rule
sections.content:
Under established legal standards practiced by banks and the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, an unassailable title search requires tracing ownership back a minimum of twenty-five (25) years through the chain of previous title deeds (বায়া দলিল / Baya Dalil):

  1. Root of Title: Tracing the land back to the recorded tenant (রায়ত) in the State Acquisition (SA) or Cadastral Survey (CS) Khatian.
  2. Every Intervening Transfer: Inspecting every single Sale Deed (সাফ কবলা), Gift Deed (হেবা), Partition Deed (বন্টননামা), or Succession Inheritance occurring over the last 25 years.
  3. Mathematical Acreage Consistency: Ensuring that the acreage transferred in each deed exactly matches the acreage owned. If an ancestor owned 20 decimals but historical deeds show transfers totaling 30 decimals, the excess 10 decimals are completely void.
  4. Absence of Ownership Gaps: Any missing link in the chain creates a cloud on title, leaving the purchaser vulnerable to future ejectment suits.

sections.h2: 3. Four Generations of Land Surveys: CS, SA, RS, and City Survey / BS Explained
sections.content:
Understanding the historical progression of land revenue surveys is mandatory for every serious real estate investor:

  • CS (Cadastral Survey 1888–1940): The foundational British-era survey. Highly accurate, accompanied by hand-drawn mouza maps. Regarded in courts as the primary baseline of title.
  • SA (State Acquisition Survey 1956): Prepared following the abolition of the Zamindari system under the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950. Crucial for establishing who held lawful tenancy after 1950.
  • RS (Revisional Survey 1965–1990): The revisional survey conducted across Bangladesh to correct SA errors and reflect modern possession. Holds immense evidentiary weight in civil courts.
  • City Survey / BS (Bangladesh Survey 1990–Present): The ongoing modern survey. In Dhaka, it is known as City Survey (ঢাকা মহানগরি জরিপ). While modern, City Survey records frequently contain bureaucratic errors; a City Survey Khatian alone does NOT confer title unless supported by RS and SA title deeds.

sections.h2: 4. Step-by-Step Remote Verification of Digital Khatians (eporcha.gov.bd)
sections.content:
The Ministry of Land's official portal eporcha.gov.bd allows expats to inspect and order certified copies of land survey records online from anywhere in the world:

  1. Access Portal: Visit eporcha.gov.bd or land.gov.bd.
  2. Geographical Navigation: Select Division (বিভাগ), District (জেলা), Upazila/Thana, and Mouza (মৌজা with JL Number).
  3. Survey Selection: Choose the Khatian type: CS, SA, RS, or BS/City Survey.
  4. Search Query: Search by Khatian number, Dag (Plot) number, or Owner's name (মালিকের নাম).
  5. Data Cross-Check: Verify: (a) Does the seller's ancestor appear as the recorded tenant? (b) Does the recorded land share (অংশ) equal the land being sold? (c) Are there adverse remarks (মন্তব্য কলাম) indicating acquisition, vested property, or government mortgage?
  6. Certified Copy Application: Submit an online application for an official Certified Copy (সার্টিফাইড কপি) bearing digital QR-code verification, delivered locally to your advocate.

sections.h2: 5. How to Detect Forged e-Namjari Mutations & Counterfeit DCR Receipts
sections.content:
One of the most dangerous frauds encountered by expatriates is the production of counterfeit manual mutation slips by sellers:

The Absolute Rule: Since 2021, manual paper mutation (ম্যানুয়াল নামজারি) has been completely abolished across Bangladesh. ANY MUTATION THAT DOES NOT EXIST ON THE CENTRAL SERVER (mutation.land.gov.bd) IS FORGED AND VOID.

Digital Verification Protocol:

  • Visit mutation.land.gov.bd. Navigate to 'Application Tracking' (আবেদন ট্র্যাকিং).
  • Input Division, District, Upazila, Application Number, and NID.
  • A genuine mutation displays the complete digital approval workflow, signed orders of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), and a valid Duplicate Carbon Receipt (DCR) showing BDT 1,150 paid into the government treasury.
  • Scan the QR code on the Mutation Khatian. It must redirect directly to the official government server displaying the identical plot and owner particulars.

Never purchase property where Land Development Tax (ভূমি উন্নয়ন কর) is delinquent or unpaid:

  1. Access ldtax.gov.bd.
  2. Enter the owner's Holding Number, Mouza, and Khatian Number.
  3. A genuine tax profile displays the updated digitized Holding (ডিজিটাল হোল্ডিং), owner's name, and historical payment ledger.
  4. Ensure taxes are cleared up to the current fiscal year. If an owner claims they have paid tax but produces old paper Dakhilas without an online record, the holding is un-digitized or disputed.

sections.h2: 7. The Vital Sub-Registry Physical Audit: Volume Books & NEC Form 41
sections.content:
While online checks verify revenue records, they cannot detect secret bank mortgages or prior sales. A qualified advocate must conduct physical searches at the Sub-Registry Office:

A. Volume Book Inspection (বালাম বই তল্লাশি)

The advocate inspects the physical Volume Book where registered deeds are hand-bound and archived. The advocate matches the deed serial, registration date, stamp duty value, and vendor/vendee signatures and thumbprints against the seller's photocopy. If the Volume Book shows a different deed on that page, the seller's deed is an outright counterfeit.

B. Non-Encumbrance Certificate (NEC - দায়মুক্ত সনদ)

Under Section 57 of the Registration Act 1908 and Form 41 of the Registration Rules, your advocate files an application for a formal 12 to 25-year Search and Non-Encumbrance Certificate:

  • The Sub-Registrar conducts a comprehensive search across all transaction registers for that specific Mouza, Khatian, and Dag.
  • If no prior sales, mortgages, or court attachments exist, the Sub-Registrar issues an official seal-embossed Non-Encumbrance Certificate (Form 41) certifying that the property is unencumbered.

sections.h2: 8. Vetting Developers & Housing Societies (RAJUK, CDA, RDA Clearances)
sections.content:
If purchasing an apartment or housing plot in Dhaka from a real estate developer, verify the following mandatory regulatory clearances:

  • REHAB Membership: Verify that the developer is an enrolled member of the Real Estate & Housing Association of Bangladesh.
  • RAJUK / Development Authority Project Approval: Under the Private Residential Land Development Rules 2004, no developer can advertise or sell plots without formal layout approval from RAJUK (Dhaka), CDA (Chattogram), or RDA (Rajshahi).
  • Building Plan Sanction (অনুমোদিত নকশা): Verify the approved architectural drawing, building height, floor area ratio (FAR), and fire/civil aviation NOCs.
  • Landowner-Developer Power of Attorney: If buying from a developer developing land on joint-venture, verify the registered Irrevocable Power of Attorney executed by the landowner in favor of the developer. Ensure the specific flat being purchased falls within the developer's allocated share.

sections.h2: 9. Red-Flag Categories: Khas, Vested Property, Waqf, and LA Cases
sections.content:
Immediately abort the transaction if your due diligence reveals any of the following fatal encumbrances:

  • Government Khas Land (সরকারি খাস জমি): Land owned exclusively by the government under Section 86 of the SAT Act 1950. Any private deed for Khas land is void ab initio.
  • Vested Property 'Ka' Schedule: Encumbered under Vested Property legislation. Cannot be sold without a formal Tribunal release decree.
  • Waqf / Debottar Religious Property: Islamic Waqf or Hindu Debottar land cannot be alienated without prior sanction from the Waqf Administrator or District Judge.
  • Land Acquisition (L.A. Case - অধিগ্রহণ): Check whether the Deputy Commissioner's Land Acquisition Branch has issued gazette notifications under the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Act 2017 for roads, metro rail, or public infrastructure.
  • Wetland / Flood Retention Zone: Land classified as water-body or flood retention zone under the Natural Water Reservoir Conservation Act 2000 cannot be land-filled or developed.

sections.h2: 10. Standard Advocate Title Search & Legal Opinion Report Structure
sections.content:
Before remitting any earnest money from abroad, demand a formal written Legal Search Report & Title Opinion (স্বত্ব মতামত প্রতিবেদন) signed by an enrolled advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. The report must contain:

  1. Executive Summary: Unambiguous opinion stating whether the title is Marketable, Free from Encumbrance, and Safe for Purchase.
  2. Chain of Title Analysis: Chronological table linking CS & SA Khatians to present ownership deeds.
  3. Survey & Mutation Verification: Analysis of RS, City Survey, e-Namjari, DCR, and online tax Dakhilas.
  4. Sub-Registry Search Findings: Report on Volume Book inspection and NEC Form 41 status.
  5. Statutory Clearances: Verification of RAJUK/CDA, environmental, and non-acquisition status.
  6. Specific Cautions & Recommendations: Mandatory conditions precedent to be inserted in the contract for sale (বায়নাপত্র).

sections.h2: 11. Real-Life Case Study: Saving a UK Expat BDT 3.5 Crore from a Forged Plot Deal
sections.content:
Background: Mr. Shafiqul Alam, a businessman in Manchester, UK, negotiated to purchase a prime 5-katha commercial plot in Uttara Sector 14, Dhaka for BDT 3.5 Crore. The seller produced impressive manual deeds, an RS Porcha in his name, and a recent tax receipt, demanding a BDT 50 Lakh non-refundable booking advance.

Chamber Due Diligence Uncovered:

  1. Our advocate conducted an e-Porcha search, discovering that the seller's RS Porcha was counterfeit; the actual recorded tenant in government archives was the Ministry of Housing and Public Works (Khas land).
  2. A physical Volume Book search at the Sub-Registry revealed that the seller's 1994 registered deed number actually corresponded to a completely different plot in Savar.
  3. The seller was operating under a forged manual mutation slip that had zero presence on mutation.land.gov.bd.
  4. We halted the wire transfer immediately, saving Mr. Shafiqul BDT 3.5 Crore ($300,000 USD) and referred the fraud syndicate to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for prosecution under the Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023.

faqs.question: Can I verify land ownership in Bangladesh online without hiring a lawyer?
faqs.answer: You can perform preliminary checks on eporcha.gov.bd and mutation.land.gov.bd, but online databases do not show secret bank mortgages or prior un-mutated sales. A physical Sub-Registry Volume Book search and NEC by an advocate are indispensable.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a Khatian and a Dalil in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: A Dalil (Deed) is the legal transfer contract executed between parties at the Sub-Registry. A Khatian (Record of Rights / Porcha) is the official government land revenue survey record reflecting title, plot boundaries, and tax assessment.

faqs.question: How do I know if a property is mortgaged to a commercial bank in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: An advocate must conduct a Non-Encumbrance Certificate (NEC Form 41) search at the Sub-Registry Office and cross-verify through bank panel lawyers with Credit Information Bureau (CIB) records.

faqs.question: What is a Baya Dalil (বায়া দলিল)?
faqs.answer: A Baya Dalil (previous deed / chain deed) is any historical registered transfer deed through which the current seller or their predecessor acquired title. A complete chain spanning 25 years is required to prove unclouded title.

faqs.question: Can a housing developer sell a plot without RAJUK approval in Dhaka?
faqs.answer: No. Under the Private Residential Land Development Rules 2004, selling or advertising unapproved housing plots is illegal and punishable with criminal imprisonment and demolition.

faqs.question: How much does a professional Title Search and Legal Opinion report cost?
faqs.answer: Depending on the complexity of the chain of title, number of previous deeds, and registry searches, advocate fees typically range from BDT 25,000 to BDT 60,000 ($250–$600 USD).

faqs.question: What is a DCR receipt in land mutation?
faqs.answer: DCR (Duplicate Carbon Receipt) is the official government treasury receipt issued upon paying the BDT 1,150 mutation fee, proving that the mutation was processed lawfully through the Assistant Commissioner (Land) office.

faqs.question: Can I buy land in Bangladesh if the seller has not completed e-Namjari?
faqs.answer: Never. Under Section 17 of the Registration Act 1908, Sub-Registrars are legally barred from registering a sale deed unless the seller's name is mutated in the government e-Namjari database with an up-to-date Khatian.
